‭Resolution Speeches - JMUN Conference XLV‬
‭Resolution I - 1‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, while the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭does believe that resolution I-1 offers a way of protection to journalists in Haiti, it‬
‭does not clarify which journalists would get the bodyguards. As Haiti has hundreds‬
‭of news outlets, Bangladesh believes it is important to clarify which outlets would‬
‭qualify for the bodyguards.‬
‭Additionally, Bangladesh believes that the press companies should be required to‬
‭cover 25% of the cost of the bodyguards because even though Bangladesh is‬
‭committed to a free press without censorship, media companies should be required to‬
‭partially pay for the protection of their employees. Having said this, Bangladesh‬
‭supports the resolution as long as there is a list determined by local Haitian‬
‭government officials along with 6th committee and UNESCO officials of which‬
‭news outlets are worthy of getting the bodyguards, and the news outlets are required‬
‭to cover at least 25% of the cost. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to‬
‭the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I - 2‬
‭While the People’s Republic of Bangladesh firmly believes in the freedom of‬
‭education without censorship, resolution I-2 does not propose an effective solution‬
‭to help promote education without censorship. Bangladesh acknowledges that‬
‭academic censorship is especially harmful because it discourages children from‬
‭seeking the truth. Resolution I-2 is not effective at discouraging censorship because‬
‭there is no plan if a country decides to censor the international website, and the‬
‭resolution is unrealistic by stating that it will provide resources to “every‬
‭individual.” Having said this, Bangladesh regrettably must oppose resolution I-2.‬
‭Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I - 3‬
‭While the People’s Republic of Bangladesh strongly condemns China’s censorship‬
‭of education, resolution I-3 is not an effective way of ending censorship in China.‬
‭This resolution does not have a way of determining which websites should be‬
‭uncensored and it does not specify the amount of funding that will come from‬
‭UNESCO. Additionally, this resolution does not specify which countries would be‬
‭asked to place sanctions on China if they do not comply with not censoring the‬
‭websites. All in all, due to the unclear sections of this resolution, Bangladesh must‬
‭regrettably oppose resolution I-3. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time‬
‭to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I - 4‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, while the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭promotes the freedom of the press, Russia’s press censorship law protects its‬
‭citizens from false information. About ten million Russian citizens watch Russian‬
‭news which shows how important the freedom of journalism is. Resolution I-4 is‬
‭too harsh on journalists, as no journalists shall be arrested if they report false‬
‭information. Additionally, instead of the Russian government determining what‬
‭news is fake, a UN oversight board will determine that by using international law‬
‭and best judgment, and a maximum of three Russian governmental officials are‬
‭allowed on the board. In conclusion, Bangladesh supports resolution I-4 as long as‬
‭no journalists are arrested and a UN oversight board determines what is fake news.‬
‭Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I-5‬
‭Honorable chairs, while the People’s Republic of Bangladesh believes learning‬
‭without censorship is crucial, resolution I-5 is not an effective way of ending‬
‭censorship of education in China. Resolution I-5 does not specify which countries‬
‭other than China would not be included in the commission and it does not specify‬
‭what the commission would exactly do. Due to this, Bangladesh must oppose‬
‭resolution I-5. Thank you, and I yield the rest of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I-6‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭strongly condemns race censorship in the United States. Minority populations are‬
‭statistically much less likely to have access to educational materials, which makes‬
‭it especially important to end race censorship. Additionally, according to the‬
‭American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), there are new bills aimed at banning the‬
‭Critical Race Theory which is a piece of education that informs students of how‬
‭systemic racism is “deeply rooted” in American society. Resolution I-6 proposes an‬
‭effective solution to ending race censorship by restoring banned books and calling‬
‭on states to implement the 1619 Project. Bangladesh also encourages Kenya to‬
‭work with United States government officials to reverse the bill which is targeted‬
‭at ending the teaching of critical race theory in grades Kindergarten through 12th.‬
‭Having said this, Bangladesh happily supports resolution I-6. Thank you, and I‬
‭yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I-7‬
‭Honorable chairs, while the People’s Republic of Bangladesh acknowledges the‬
‭rather extreme censorship of education in China, resolution I-7 does not offer an‬
‭adequate solution to help to end the censorship of education in China. The‬
‭resolution does not outline which “things” would be included in the checklist and‬
‭how the checklist would be qualified as “good.” Additionally, there is no follow-up‬
‭plan if China does not use the checklist or unban the books. All in all, due to the‬
‭lack of elaboration in the resolution, Bangladesh must regrettably oppose‬
‭resolution I-7. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I-8‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh values‬
‭access to books worldwide. Books are an important part of education, especially‬
‭because many informational books are peer-reviewed and they are great sources of‬
‭accurate information for students. Additionally, according to the National‬
‭Children’s Book and Literacy Alliance “Books help kids develop basic language‬
‭skills and profoundly expand their vocabularies” while they also promote critical‬
‭thinking. Resolution I-8 offers a great solution for countries who unnecessarily ban‬
‭books to create a fair system of rating and unbanning the books. Keeping in mind‬
‭that there are tens of millions of books in existence, it is unrealistic to rate‬
‭everyone, therefore instead of rating every single book, only books that are in‬
‭schools should be rated. Assuming this amendment is included in the resolution,‬
‭Bangladesh will happily support resolution I-8. Thank you, and I yield the‬
‭remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution I-10‬
‭Honorable chairs, while the People’s Republic of Bangladesh acknowledges that‬
‭the academic censorship in China fabricates people’s political views, resolution‬
‭I-10 does not offer a proper solution to ending academic censorship in China. This‬
‭resolution leaves the solution up to non-governmental organizations to solve the‬
‭problems which posses an issue because governments have more power than‬
‭NGOs, and since China is likely to not end its academic censorship laws without‬
‭force, NGOs can not force governments to do anything. Therefore Bangladesh‬
‭regrettably opposes resolution I-10. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my‬
‭time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution II-1‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, Bangladesh is committed to the protection‬
‭of cultural and Heritage sites and items. Bangladesh has two UNESCO identified‬
‭world heritage sites and our neighboring country, India, has 33 UNESCO identified‬
‭world heritage sites, therefore it is of the utmost importance to protect world‬
‭heritage sites. Resolution II-1 allows for a safe location for historical artifacts and‬
‭implements plans to protect cultural and heritage sites. Additionally, Bangladesh‬
‭asks for an amendment to resolution II-1 so that an additional three million dollars‬
‭from the world bank is used to repair damaged world heritage sites. Assuming this‬
‭amendment is implemented in the resolution, Bangladesh will happily support‬
‭resolution II-1. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution II-2‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, with the ongoing conflict in the Middle‬
‭East, it is very important that cultural heritage is protected, especially during times‬
‭of conflict. At present, all of the countries currently at war, in or around the Middle‬
‭East collectively have 55 heritage sites, and about 20% of those are at high risk.‬
‭Due to the extreme urgency of this matter, Bangladesh suggests an amendment to‬
‭the timeline in Resolution II-2 in part 4. a. - Collaborations should start between‬
‭the Middle Eastern countries currently at war (including Iran, Iraq, Syria, Egypt,‬
‭Israel, Saudi Arabia, Afghanistan, Yemen, and the United Arab Emirates) and the‬
‭United States of America to structure a military plan by January first, 2023 and the‬
‭groups should start to be assembled by March 1st, 2024 which will allow for‬
‭enough time for a decisive military plan while also acting with a sense of urgency.‬
‭Given that these amendments are included in the resolution, Bangladesh will‬
‭happily support resolution II-2. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to‬
‭the chairs.‬
‭Resolution II-3‬
‭Honorable chairs, even though the People’s Republic of Bangladesh strongly‬
‭supports the protection of cultural heritage, resolution II-3 does not effectively help‬
‭countries protect against the destruction of cultural heritage. Resolution II-3 does‬
‭not have a specific timeline or spending amount, along with a specific job‬
‭description of the guards which therefore makes the resolution incomplete. Also,‬
‭the resolution would only give the funding for protecting cultural heritage sites to‬
‭countries who contribute to this initiative, which means that this resolution does‬
‭not offer a solution for poor countries, which would benefit the most from this‬
‭resolution as they do not have the resources to protect their cultural heritage. 49 of‬
‭the 52 at-risk heritage sites that are in danger are in economically unstable‬
‭countries which shows how crucial it is for the countries to get the funding to‬
‭protect their cultural heritage sites, even if they can not contribute. All in all, due to‬
‭the lack of support for poor countries, Bangladesh must regrettably oppose‬
‭resolution II-3. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution II-4‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭recognizes the pressing issue of at-risk cultural and heritage sites in Ukraine due to‬
‭the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. Over 127 cultural sites on the UNESCO‬
‭cultural heritage list have been damaged by the ongoing conflict between Russia‬
‭and Ukraine. Additionally, both countries have signed the‬‭1954 Hauge Convention‬
‭Act‬‭which makes damaging cultural and world heritage‬‭sites a war crime.‬
‭Resolution II-4 offers an effective way of repairing damaged cultural sites and‬
‭protecting cultural sites from being further damaged. As Bangladesh views this‬
‭matter as urgent, Bangladesh requests an amendment to be made to the timeline for‬
‭when the cultural sites shall be repaired - instead of by 2040, all damaged cultural‬
‭and heritage sites in Ukraine shall be repaired by December 31st, 2035 which will‬
‭allow for approximately 13 years for the repairs to take place. Having said this,‬
‭assuming the amendment is made to the timeline, Bangladesh strongly supports‬
‭resolution II-4. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution II-5‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭acknowledges the pressing issue of persevering at-risk cultural and heritage sites in‬
‭Lviv, Ukraine during the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Resolution‬
‭II-5 effectively offers a partial solution to protect at-risk cultural artifacts in‬
‭Ukraine. Bangladesh believes that historical artifacts belong in museums in the‬
‭country that they belong to, therefore Bangladesh requests an amendment to‬
‭resolution II-5. Instead of artifacts being permanently relocated to trusted museums‬
‭in Europe if there is not a stable location for the artifacts in Ukraine after ten years,‬
‭the artifacts should be temporarily dispersed to museums around Europe after five‬
‭years but returned to Ukraine when Ukraine is in a stable position to take the‬
‭artifacts. Additionally, Bangladesh proposes 3 million dollars (IN USD) from the‬
‭world bank to pay for the moving trucks and ensure the safe transfer of historical‬
‭artifacts. Assuming these amendments are made, Bangladesh supports resolution‬
‭II-5. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution III-1‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭realizes the importance of comprehensive sexual education and the problems that‬
‭are created when a child does not receive comprehensive sexual education. As a‬
‭study from the University of Albany states “abstinence-only (sex) education‬
‭programs don’t reduce teen pregnancy rates, and in some areas, have the opposite‬
‭effect.” Additionally, countries that teach sexual education have lower teen‬
‭pregnancy rates than countries that don’t. Resolution III-1 offers an effective‬
‭solution to address the global lack of sexual education as it encourages countries to‬
‭provide incentives to teach sexual education and the resolution creates a program‬
‭that will raise awareness about the global lack of sexual education. Bangladesh‬
‭asks that the initial rollout of the program be completed by January 1st, 2025.‬
‭Additionally, Bangladesh requests that an additional website be created in‬
‭partnership with the World Health Organization that includes videos with‬
‭comprehensive sexual education taught by WHO sexual education specialists.‬
‭Assuming these two amendments are made, Bangladesh happily supports‬
‭resolution III-1. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution III-2‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭recognizes that the lack of sexual education in the United States of America is a‬
‭pressing issue. Bangladesh acknowledges that Norway’s teen pregnancy rate is 5‬
‭for every 1,000 teens get pregnant (aged 15-19) and Norway teaches‬
‭comprehensive sexual education whereas the United States teen pregnancy rate is‬
‭16 for every 1,000 teens get pregnant (aged 15-19). This proves that teaching‬
‭comprehensive sexual education leads to lower teen pregnancy rates. Resolution‬
‭III-2 effectively offers a solution to ensure that sex education is mandated in the‬
‭United States in grades 6-12. Having said this, Bangladesh strongly supports‬
‭resolution III-2. Thank you, and I yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution III-3‬
‭Honorable chairs, while the People’s Republic of Bangladesh acknowledges the‬
‭substandard sex education in China, resolution III-3 does not offer an effective‬
‭solution to ensure that children in Chinese schools are taught sexual education.‬
‭Resolution III-3 does not include a plan if China decides not to tech more‬
‭comprehensive sexual education and follow the guidelines outlined in this‬
‭resolution which therefore relies on China to implement the solutions by‬
‭themselves without any repercussions from other governments if they don’t. Also,‬
‭resolution III-3 does not include a timeline for the plan to be implemented.‬
‭Therefore Bangladesh regrettably must oppose resolution III-3. Thank you, and I‬
‭yield the remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Resolution III-4‬
‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of Bangladesh‬
‭realizes that HIV education, treatment, and prevention is of the utmost importance‬
‭in Africa. HIV is a sexually transmitted disease that adversely affects one’s life‬
‭forever and in some cases can cause death, and without proper education and‬
‭testing, another HIV epidemic can occur, especially in some of the developing‬
‭countries in Africa. Resolution III-4 offers solutions for both HIV testing and‬
‭education in Africa. Bangladesh requests both 5% of the World Health‬
‭Organizations' available yearly funds (that are applicable for this cause) of 3.338‬
‭billion and 20% of the US’s 6.8 billion global HIV available funding to be used for‬
‭testing and research along with 5% of UNAIDS 242 million dollar budget to be‬
‭used for HIV education. Assuming that these funding requests are added to the‬
‭resolution, Bangladesh happily supports resolution III-4. Thank you, and I yield the‬
‭remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
‭Crisis -‬‭Honorable chairs and fellow delegates, the People’s Republic of‬
‭Bangladesh acknowledges the ongoing conflict between North Korea and the‬
‭United States and is concerned about how there may be increased education‬
‭censorship or heritage sites at risk during this trying time. Bangladesh is concerned‬
‭that the United States, Russia, and China are spreading propaganda to mitigate the‬
‭concerns of their citizens. While Bangladesh believes that trying to comfort a‬
‭country's citizens in a time of crisis is crucial, Bangladesh is opposed to spreading‬
‭propaganda and it is prepared to partner with our allies to ensure that no further‬
‭propaganda is spread. Additionally, Bangladesh is concerned that‬‭heritage sites‬
‭belonging to the Islamic Religion are at risk due to the rising power of the Hezbollah military‬
‭forces in Middle Eastern countries. Bangladesh asks for other countries' cooperation in making‬
‭sure no propaganda is spread and heritage sites remain safe. Thank you, and I yield the‬
‭remainder of my time to the chairs.‬
